outcomes: The result was Bushfire, a prototype early-warning platform tailored to local needs and designed to strengthen both formal and informal communication. summary: In Victoria, Australia, The People and the Fire Tree: Co-Designing a Bushfire Early Warning System is a monitoring and adaptive management initiative. The project used participatory co-design methods through five workshops with residents of a rural, fire-prone community in Victoria. Participants developed two systems: The Fire Tree—a visual tool for tracking fire threat levels—and The People System—a platform integrating official government resources with informal local communication networks. The collaboration involved researchers from Swinburne University’s Centre for Design Innovation and Centre for Social Impact, emphasizing lived experience, local insight, and institutional coordination. The case addresses wildfire and Smoke, Flooding. Available materials report the result was Bushfire, a prototype early-warning platform tailored to local needs and designed to strengthen both formal and informal communication. The project increased residents’ sense of agency and confidence in preparedness while creating a tool that bridges gaps between community response and institutional systems.
title: The People and the Fire Tree: Co-Designing a Bushfire Early Warning System
transferability: As wildfires intensify across Washington, this case offers a model for community-based early warning systems that reflect local context and build public trust. Integrating community input with agency data, as done in Victoria, could help Washington better tailor alerts and preparedness tools, particularly for rural and Tribal communities. The emphasis on co-production, equity, and local communication networks aligns with Washington’s goals of inclusive, community-led climate adaptation.
